newsitem.title: USA: Texas power holds steady, off-peak talked higher.
newsitem.headline: Texas power holds steady, off-peak talked higher.

text.p: Bulk wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) held steady again Thursday although off-peak next day prices were talked higher, industry sources said.
Mild temperatures seemed to be the only news to drive the ERCOT market, which has held relatively steady through most of the week, the brokers and marketers said.
Peak, firm electricity in ERCOT for Thursday delivery was said to be talked steady at $23.00-24.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.

Off-peak ERCOT power for Friday delivery was thinly discussed at $15.00-18.00 from Wednesday discussion at $14.00-17.00, with sources citing the cool overnight weather and some generation outages as pushing values higher.

November peak ERCOT power was talked lower at $21.00-21.50 from $22.00-22.50 earlier this week, while December was said to be in the $21.50-23.00 range from quotes at $23.00-24.00 earlier this week, the sources said.
Expectations of milder fall temperatures and resulting decreased demand were said to be putting downward pressure on the longer-term prices.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
